checkmate-basics.title: Checkmate basics
checkmate-basics.summary: Deliver mate with a rook and a queen.
checkmate-basics.s1: Checkmate ends the game: the king is attacked and has no way to escape, block or capture the attacker.
checkmate-basics.s2: This is a back-rank mate. The rook gives check along the first rank and the black king is trapped behind its own pawns.
checkmate-basics.s3: Your turn: the black king is boxed in by its pawns. Find the checkmate in one move.
checkmate-basics.s4: The king and queen work together. Find the move that checks the king while it cannot capture the queen.

forks.title: Forks
forks.summary: Attack two pieces at once with a knight.
forks.s1: A fork is a single move that attacks two or more enemy pieces. Knights are excellent at it because they jump.
forks.s2: The knight on f7 checks the king and attacks the queen at the same time. Black must save the king, then White takes the queen.
forks.s3: Find the knight move that attacks both the king and the queen.

opening-principles.title: Opening principles
opening-principles.summary: Control the center and develop your pieces.
opening-principles.s1: In the opening, fight for the center, develop your knights and bishops, and get your king to safety.
opening-principles.s2: Play a good first move that fights for the center or develops a piece.
opening-principles.s3: Black has taken space in the center. Develop a knight toward the center.
opening-principles.s4: Well done. Remember: center, development, king safety.

studio.warnBody: This studio builds board themes from colors, gradients, your own textures and the built-in effects. It is not the best way to make themes, and it cannot make 3D themes, animated pieces or rendered pieces: those need art tools such as Blender. Use it to start and to learn the format, then edit theme.json by hand.
studio.previewNote: The preview uses your current pieces.
studio.name: Name
studio.author: Author
studio.needName: Give your theme a name and a valid id (lowercase letters, digits, dashes) first.
studio.bigImage: This image is larger than 6 MB.
studio.guideFormat: A theme is a .cctheme file: a ZIP archive with a theme.json at its root plus images (png, webp, jpg, svg). It is purely declarative: no code of any kind. Everything is validated when you import it: unknown fields, out-of-range values, unsafe paths, fake images and oversized files are rejected with a precise message.
studio.guideFields:
format (must be 1), id, name, version (1.0.0), author, license, description. Then board and/or pieces.
board.view.tilt: 0–65° camera tilt (0 = top view). board.scene: background (color, gradient, texture). board.frame: width in squares, paint, bevel, glow. board.squares.light / dark: color, gradient or texture, plus gloss, bevel, grid. board.highlights: style fill / ring / glow and colors. board.ambient: sweep, particles, vignette.
pieces.source: path pattern with {piece} (wK, bQ…) and optionally {res} (1x, 2x, 4x). pieces.baseSize, scale, anchor, offsetY, shadow, idle (float / breathe / glow / frames), motion (slide / arc / hop, easing, lift, squash, trail, impact), capture (fade / burst / shatter / dissolve), frames (sprite strips).
studio.guide3dTitle: How to make a 3D theme (the studio can't)
studio.guide3d:
1. Model the 12 pieces in Blender or any 3D tool. Use one camera for all of them (for example 50° above the horizon), a transparent background and the piece foot always at the same height in the image.
2. Render each piece as a square image at 1024 px, then export 512 px and 256 px versions. Save them as webp (or png) in pieces/4x, pieces/2x and pieces/1x named wP, wN, wB, wR, wQ, wK, bP … bK.
3. In theme.json set pieces.source to pieces/{res}/{piece}.webp, resolutions to ["1x","2x","4x"], baseSize to 256, anchor.y to where the foot sits in the image (for example 0.85) and scale so tall pieces fit (1.1 to 1.5). Do not bake a shadow: the app draws a soft one (pieces.shadow).
4. Board: paint two seamless square textures (light, dark) at 1024 px, or render them top-down. The app tilts the board itself: set board.view.tilt to 90° minus the camera elevation of your pieces so that board and pieces share the same angle (50° elevation → tilt 40).
5. Animated pieces: render an idle loop as one horizontal strip of frames per piece, then set pieces.frames {count, fps} and pieces.idle.style to frames.
6. Zip the contents of the folder (theme.json must be at the root of the archive, not inside a subfolder), rename the file to .cctheme and import it here. If something is wrong the import tells you exactly what.
Limits: 64 MB per archive, images up to 8192 px and 36 megapixels, png / webp / jpg / svg only. Real-time 3D models (glTF) and shaders are not part of format 1: they need a WebGL renderer and a separate security review.
